narr: Thunderstorms developed during the evening of July 14th and continued into the early morning of July 15th, as they moved across all of northern and central Illinois. Nine tornadoes occurred, along with widespread wind damage. In the City of Chicago, there were 2,810 tree emergency calls and 1,430 calls for tree debris. Localized flash flooding also occurred, for a second night in a row in the Rockford area.
ev: Main Street was impassable with approximately 10 inches of water between Indiana Street and Roosevelt Road.

Around 2115 CST, a pickup truck with two people inside attempted to drive through moving flood waters in a parking lot due to flash flooding of Keith Creek near Charles Street and 22nd Street. The pickup truck was swept away by the flood waters. The driver was able to escape but was swept underneath a culvert at 22nd Street before being rescued. A 76 year old passenger became trapped in the pickup truck and drowned.
Multiple reports of street flooding were received from southwest Naperville.

Thunderstorms producing torrential rainfall moved across southern Winnebago County and Rockford during the evening of July 14th producing significant flash flooding. Street flooding with stalled vehicles were reported all across Rockford. Multiple cars were flooded along roadways near the Alpine Dam where water levels reached two feet below the spillway. Widespread street flooding was reported near Gorham Place and Barrington Road and also near 11th Street and Broadway Street. Significant erosion occurred near roadways and parking lots at the Swedish American Hospital on State Street. Numerous basements were flooded.
